findings.claim: AssignmentSource.queued defaults to timezone.now(), which is evaluated once at class definition/import time. Every instance created without an explicit value therefore shares the same stale timestamp instead of getting its own creation time.

verifier.reason: src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py:18 (patch line 80) sets `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` as a plain dataclass default. Python evaluates it once when the class is defined, so every instance built without a value, including through `from_integration` (lines 20-25), gets the import-time timestamp. The fix is `field(default_factory=timezone.now)`.

findings.claim: to_dict() uses asdict(), which leaves queued as a datetime object. Serializing the dict to JSON as task kwargs can raise TypeError.

verifier.reason: `to_dict()` does leave `queued` as a datetime (assignment_source.py:89-90), but these task kwargs are never turned into JSON. Celery is set to use pickle here (src/sentry/conf/server.py:739-741: `CELERY_TASK_SERIALIZER = "pickle"`, accept only pickle), pickle handles datetimes fine, and the `sync_assignee_outbound` task (sync_assignee_outbound.py:15-21) does not switch to another serializer.

findings.claim: from_dict does not type-check or convert queued on deserialisation, so under a JSON serializer it comes back as a str.

verifier.reason: `from_dict` just calls `cls(**input_dict)` and never parses or checks `queued` (src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py:93-97), so a JSON round trip would bring it back as a string. In practice Sentry uses pickle (`CELERY_TASK_SERIALIZER = "pickle"` at src/sentry/conf/server.py:739), which keeps the datetime, and nothing reads `.queued` anywhere, so it has no effect today.

findings.claim: The test method name test_from_dict_inalid_data contains a typo; it should be test_from_dict_invalid_data.

verifier.reason: The patch adds a test method named `test_from_dict_inalid_data` (change.patch:277; tests/sentry/integrations/services/test_assignment_source.py:13). 'inalid' is a misspelling of 'invalid'.

findings.claim: The test test_from_dict_empty_array passes an empty dict, not an array, so its name misdescribes the case.

verifier.reason: In change.patch:272-275, test_from_dict_empty_array sets `data: dict[str, Any] = {}`, which is an empty dict, and passes it to AssignmentSource.from_dict. No array is involved, so the name describes the case wrongly.

findings.claim: The abstract sync_status_outbound has an assignment_source parameter that no caller passes and no implementation reads.

verifier.reason: The patch adds `assignment_source` to the abstract `sync_status_outbound` (src/sentry/integrations/mixins/issues.py:416), but its only caller (src/sentry/integrations/tasks/sync_status_outbound.py:44-46) passes just three positional arguments. None of the implementations use it: jira/integration.py:990, jira_server/integration.py:1090 and vsts/issues.py:266 take only `**kwargs`, and example/integration.py:161 has no such parameter.

findings.claim: The abstract contract is inconsistent: sync_assignee_outbound declares the source parameter, but sync_status_outbound does not follow the same pattern.

verifier.reason: The claim has it backwards. In src/sentry/integrations/mixins/issues.py:397-403, the abstract sync_assignee_outbound has no source parameter (only external_issue, user, assign, **kwargs), while sync_status_outbound at :411-418 is the one the patch gave `assignment_source`. So the contract is inconsistent, but the reverse of what is claimed: the parameter landed on the status method while the task calls sync_assignee_outbound with assignment_source= (sync_assignee_outbound.py:138-140), and that call only works through **kwargs.

findings.claim: Status-sync cycles are not protected. tasks/sync_status_outbound.py calls should_sync("outbound_status") without a source argument, so only assignee sync gets loop protection.

verifier.reason: src/sentry/integrations/tasks/sync_status_outbound.py:19 takes no source argument, and line 43 calls `installation.should_sync("outbound_status")` with no `sync_source`. So the same-integration check added in mixins/issues.py (patch lines 35-36) only runs for assignee sync, which passes `parsed_assignment_source` in sync_assignee_outbound.py. The patch adds an `assignment_source` parameter to the abstract `sync_status_outbound`, but nothing ever passes a value to it.

findings.claim: ExampleIntegration.sync_status_outbound has no **kwargs, so it raises TypeError when called with the new assignment_source argument.

verifier.reason: ExampleIntegration.sync_status_outbound at src/sentry/integrations/example/integration.py:161 does lack **kwargs, but nothing passes it assignment_source. The patch only adds the parameter to the abstract signature in mixins/issues.py, and the only caller (src/sentry/integrations/tasks/sync_status_outbound.py:44-46) still passes just three positional arguments, so no TypeError can occur.

findings.claim: No test drives sync_group_assignee_inbound end to end to show that the source integration is skipped while a second integration still syncs.

verifier.reason: The only tests that call sync_group_assignee_inbound for real (tests/sentry/models/test_groupassignee.py:289-388) each set up one integration and never check outbound syncing, and the new test (test_groupassignee.py:180) calls GroupAssignee.objects.assign directly with one integration. The webhook tests (jira/test_webhooks.py:44, jira_server/test_webhooks.py:68, vsts/test_webhooks.py:103) replace sync_group_assignee_inbound with a mock.

findings.claim: No test covers deassign with a matching source integration.

verifier.reason: The patch adds a matching-source test only for assign (tests/sentry/models/test_groupassignee.py:~207-218). The deassign outbound test (line 273) passes no assignment_source. test_assignee_sync_inbound_deassign (lines 349-388) reaches deassign through sync_group_assignee_inbound but runs outside self.tasks() and never mocks or checks sync_assignee_outbound, so it does not test that the outbound sync is skipped.

findings.claim: The new task kwarg assignment_source_dict causes TypeError on old workers during a rolling deploy, so assignee sync is lost.

verifier.reason: sync_group_assignee_outbound always puts an "assignment_source_dict" key in the task kwargs, even when it is None (src/sentry/integrations/utils/sync.py:136-145). A worker still running the old `sync_assignee_outbound(external_issue_id, user_id, assign)` signature will therefore raise TypeError. However, the @retry wrapper catches that error and requeues the task up to 5 times, 5 minutes apart (src/sentry/tasks/base.py:163-172; sync_assignee_outbound.py:18-22), so the sync is lost only if every retry also lands on an old worker. Usually it is just delayed.

findings.claim: from_dict catches TypeError/ValueError and returns None without logging or emitting a metric, so a malformed payload silently disables loop protection.

verifier.reason: In src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py (new file, lines 30-35 of the patch), from_dict wraps cls(**input_dict) in `except (ValueError, TypeError): return None` and neither logs nor records a metric. sync_assignee_outbound.py then passes that None to should_sync, so the integration_id check in mixins/issues.py that stops sync loops is skipped without any trace.

findings.claim: A database-backed sentry TestCase is used to test a plain dataclass that needs no DB access.

verifier.reason: tests/sentry/integrations/services/test_assignment_source.py:268-271 makes TestAssignmentSource a subclass of sentry.testutils.cases.TestCase, which is a Django test case that uses the database (src/sentry/testutils/cases.py:506). The tests only call from_dict, to_dict and the constructor of the frozen dataclass in src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py:76-97, and none of these touch the DB.

findings.claim: Both parameters (attribute, sync_source) of the default should_sync implementation are unused and flagged by Ruff.

verifier.reason: Both parameters are in fact unused in the base `should_sync` (src/sentry/integrations/mixins/issues.py, around line 66, which just returns False). But nothing would flag them: the repo has no Ruff config or dependency, and its linter is flake8 (setup.cfg:96), which has no unused-argument rule. Also, `attribute` was already unused before this patch, and a base method meant to be overridden needs these parameters to keep the same signature.

findings.claim: source_name is serialised into every task payload but never read; should_sync compares only integration_id.

verifier.reason: `source_name` is set in src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py:23 and sent to the task through `to_dict()` (utils/sync.py:141), but nothing in src/ reads `.source_name`. `should_sync` (mixins/issues.py:35) compares only `sync_source.integration_id`. One correction: the field is not in every task payload, only when an assignment source is given; otherwise the task gets None.

findings.claim: The loop guard compares integration IDs rather than external issues, so an inbound reassignment no longer propagates between two external issues linked to the same group on the same integration.

verifier.reason: In src/sentry/integrations/mixins/issues.py:389-390, should_sync returns False whenever sync_source.integration_id equals the target org_integration.integration_id. sync_group_assignee_inbound (src/sentry/integrations/utils/sync.py:96-116) tags every inbound change with only the integration ID, and sync_group_assignee_outbound (sync.py:131-145) sends it to every linked external issue. So a second issue on the same integration that is linked to the same group no longer gets the assignee, although it did before the patch.
